why: The key BST fact: an inorder traversal visits the keys in ascending order, so the k-th smallest is simply the k-th node an inorder walk visits.
hints: In what order does left subtree, node, right subtree visit the keys of a BST?
Inorder is sorted. Walk it and count; stop at the k-th visited node.
Iterative inorder: push the left spine, pop a node (count it), then push the left spine of its right child. O(h + k) time, O(h) space.
pitfalls: k is one-based: k = 1 is the minimum.
Stop as soon as you reach k; there is no need to collect the whole list.
